records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:73 — group.users.delete(user_id) passes an integer to an ActiveRecord association method that expects model instances, causing member removal to raise instead of deleting
records.rationale: The diff adds `group.users.delete(user_id)` where user_id is an Integer (`params.require(:user_id).to_i`). ActiveRecord's CollectionAssociation#delete expects model instances (or objects responding to id), not raw integers; passing an Integer will raise rather than remove the join record, breaking member removal. This mechanism is plausible from the diff, though Rails version specifics aren't fully verifiable here.

records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit has no upper bound or positive-value validation, allowing arbitrarily large membership lists to be requested and serialized
records.rationale: The diff shows `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` with no upper-bound or positive-value validation, and the new code now applies this param to ALL groups (previously the limit/offset params only applied to automatic groups). A user-supplied huge limit would serialize arbitrarily large membership lists via `group.users.limit(limit)`. This is a specific, decision-relevant input-validation gap for a public, non-admin endpoint created/widened by this diff, though not a strict correctness defect.
